title: Eikev: not by bread only (Deuteronomy 8:3)
hook: "man doth not live by bread only", the lesson of the manna

segments.voice: Yesterday, lifnim: inside the line of the law, the right and the good. Your line was beyond the letter. Today a new portion, Eikev, and a sentence people quote without knowing its home.

Man does not live by bread alone. It gets said about jobs that pay well and feel empty, about art, about weekends. It's often taken for an old proverb, or for a line from the Gospels, where Jesus quotes it in the wilderness. But it's a quotation there too. Its home is here, in Moses' farewell, and it isn't about bread in general. It's about one very specific food that fell from the sky every morning for forty years.
screen: `NOT BY BREAD ALONE.` → `A LINE PEOPLE QUOTE.` → `ITS HOME IS HERE.`

segments.voice: First the portion's name. Eikev means because, from its opening: because you listen to these laws, blessing will follow. But eikev is also the Hebrew word for heel, the same root as Jacob, who came out holding his brother's heel. Rashi plays on it: eikev points to the small commandments people tend to trample under their heels, the ones that seem minor. Then Moses turns back to the wilderness. In the old Jewish translation: "And He afflicted thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that He might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every thing that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live." Hear the order. Hunger first, then a food no one recognized. Manna couldn't be stored; it spoiled overnight, except for the Sabbath portion. You couldn't stockpile it or own it. Every morning you depended again. And the point, Moses says, was a lesson: bread is real, people need it, but life doesn't come only from what you can grow or buy or keep. In his telling, it also comes from somewhere no one controls. He adds a detail to make it vivid: "Thy raiment waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years." Forty years of walking, and their feet held. Not by bread only, Moses says. Not bread never, either. Bread, and more than bread.
screen: `EIKEV: BECAUSE, AND HEEL.` · `HUNGER, THEN A FOOD NOBODY KNEW.` · `MANNA YOU COULDN'T STORE.` · `BREAD, AND MORE THAN BREAD.` · then, large: `NOT BY BREAD ALONE.`

segments.voice: Notice your body, hungry, full or somewhere between: that's the bread part, and it's real. Then ask what you've been living on lately besides food, and what truly nourishes you that you've let go thin: a walk, an old friend, a page of something beautiful, a few minutes of quiet. Name one, and hold it the way you'd hold warm bread.
Eikev. Because, and also heel. The name of the portion, from its opening word: because you listen.
Your line: not by bread alone. The manna came one morning at a time. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Eikev is read in synagogues in late summer, and on the Sabbath two loaves are set on the table, a custom tied to the double portion of manna that fell before the Sabbath.
